questions.question: Distinguish between Speculative and Analytic Philosophy of History. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Distinguish between Speculative and Analytic Philosophy of History. [U] / [CO1] - These are two
  • branches of philosophy of history: speculative philosophy of history is about how historians of various
  • periods thought about the past. Here historian speculates what happened in the past based on evidences
  • and facts- Analytical philosophy of history is the academic study of why historians thought about their
  • past in a certain particular manner. It enquires why histo rian choose a particular way of writing history
  • or way of looking at history - The former is about the historical past, while the latter is about the
  • discipline of history.

questions.question: Analyse history as a reenactment of the past experience. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse history as a reenactment of the past experience. [An] / [CO3] – British historian RG
  • Collingwood proposed the concept of ‘reenactment’ – He argued that history is not merely a collection
  • of facts or a chronological narrative, but a complex process of mental reconstruction or "reenactment" of
  • past thoughts and experiences –It is an intellectual reimagining the cognitive landscape of a particular
  • historical moment through contextual understanding and sophisticated hermeneutic approach to
  • historical sources - Here historians must imaginatively recreate the mental processes and perspectives of
  • historical actors to truly comprehend historical events.

questions.question: Outline the biography of Marc Bloch as given by Braudel in his 'Personal Testimony'. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Outline the biography of Marc Bloch as given by Braudel in his 'Personal Testimony'. [U] / [CO2]
  • – One of the pioneer member of Annales movement – Son of eminent historian Gustav Bloch -
  • exemplary career at school and collegiate education – The Royal Touch was one of his early seminal
  • works– Bloch met Lucien Febvre at the University of Strasbourg – together they started Annales journal

questions.question: Can objectivity be considered the most cherished value in scientific research within the field of History? Critically examine. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Can objectivity be considered the most cherished value in scientific research within the
  • field of History? Critically examine. [An] / [CO1] – Though a cherished goal, achieving
  • complete objectivity in historical writing is undoubtedly challenging – Positivist notion of
  • objectivity is difficult to attain in history - History, by its nature, is a subject that cannot be
  • unbiased, objective, or mere ly factual - The question of historical objectivity is closely linked
  • with value judgment – There are many factors limiting historical objectivity including; Personal
  • and group prejudice, conflicting historical interpretations, differences in philosophical views,
  • value judgements and moral values, incomplete evidences etc… - Consultation of maximum
  • possible sources, loyalty to facts, kept chauvinistic tendencies away from historical analysis etc
  • may help in objective treatment of sources and reading - Certainly, true objectivity is not
  • attainable, but it is nonetheless a reasonable and desirable goal for historians to strive for.
